newsitem.title: JAPAN: Siemens set to advance into Japanese chip market.
newsitem.headline: Siemens set to advance into Japanese chip market.

text.p: German electronics giant Siemens AG unveiled plans on Wednesday to advance into Japan's chip market next spring. It will be the first European memory chip maker to do so.
The move is likely to further pressure domestic makers already suffering from market oversupply and price falls, industry analysts said.

Siemens KK, the firm's Japanese subsidiary, said it had acquired a majority stake in its joint venture with Fuji Electric Co Ltd and would import dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips made by Siemens to Japan through the firm.

Siemens hopes to start selling DRAM chips manufactured at its joint venture with International Business Machines Corp (IBM) in Europe in Japan as early as next year, a spokeswoman for Siemens KK said.
Siemens is the largest maker of DRAMs in Europe, with annual sales in the chip business expected to reach around 320 billion yen ($2.90 billion) in the current business year ending on September 30.
"Stepping up its presence in Japan is part of Siemens' global strategy," said Yoshimichi Takizawa, director in charge of marketing and technology at Fuji Electronic Components.
"Although Japan is the world's largest supplier of memory chips, it also accounts for 20 percent of the world market," said Takizawa.
Analysts said local chip makers were likely to face tougher competition in light of the German electronic maker's entry into the Japanese market.

"Japanese chip makers have seen a sharp increase in their inventories recently and the European firm's entry would further deteriorate the market's supply-demand conditions," said Yoshiharu Izumi, an analyst at UBS Securities Ltd.
Amid a supply glut after a worldwide slowdown in personal computer sales, chip makers have begun to slash prices.
In the last nine months, prices of DRAMs for volume users have fallen by more than 70 percent to around 1,000 yen ($9), according to industry sources.
The difficult conditions have been compounded by competition from South Korean chip makers, who have been selling their products aggressively.
UBS's Izumi also said Siemens would be a strong competitor in Japan, considering its ties with IBM, which will likely be a major buyer of Siemens' chips as well as providing technology.

Nevertheless, Takizawa said the company does not plan to immediately start marketing its memory chips aggressively, as market conditions are at a very difficult stage. But he also said the memory chip business in Japan will be important as it is the flagship product in Siemen's semiconductor operation.
Siemens KK boosted its stake in the joint venture, Fuji Electric Components Ltd from 50 percent to 80 percent, at the beginning of July, the spokeswoman said.
The venture will change its name to Siemens Components KK on October 1. Its sales are expected to reach almost six billion yen ($54.5 million) in the business year to next March. ($1=110 yen)
